- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment was >0.7 in the prior 3–5 days.
- Underestimate prices after negative sentiment (sentiment <0.3) or prolonged bearish sentiment; add 3–7% to forecast if sentiment dropped below 0.2 in last 5 days.
- Model tends to lag in downward corrections — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by adding 1–3% to avoid underestimating sharp drops.
- Overshoots after strong upward moves (e.g., >75% spike in 3-day window) — cap forecast at 10–15% below prior peak if sentiment was >0.8 for 3+ days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast shows >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment >0.6 for 5+ days, forecast should be 2–4% lower than model if true outcome shows 5–10% drop in next 3 days.
